An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

NVIDIA is seeking an EMEA Sales Senior Account Manager for Smart Spaces & Local Government. In this role, you will own strategic relationships with leading cities, public-sector organizations, and smart-space operators, positioning NVIDIA’s platforms and AI Factory strategy as the engine for modernizing public services and competitiveness across the region. You will uncover and develop new opportunities, expand NVIDIA’s regional footprint, and work with cross-functional teams to accelerate adoption of AI and Digital Twins in city environments. In the Senior Account Manager role, passionate about Enterprise Sales, you will lead strategic relationships with leading cities, local governments, and smart-space operators. You will present NVIDIA’s platform, ecosystem, and AI Factory strategy as the driving force behind improvements in public services, economic competitiveness, and citizens’ daily lives. You will identify new opportunities, expand NVIDIA’s footprint across regions, and work with cross-functional teams to accelerate AI and Digital Twin adoption in city environments.

What you will be doing:

  • Crafting revenue growth for NVIDIA’s Smart Cities, Smart Spaces, and Local Government solutions—with a focus on AI Factories, digital twins, physical infrastructure intelligence, generative AI, and computer vision.

  • Build robust pipeline and supporting governments deploy AI responsibly across mobility, urban planning, sustainability, energy efficiency, public safety, inspection, and citizen services.

  • Developing long-term relationships with senior city leaders, CIOs, CTOs, ministers, mayors’ offices, public-sector agencies, and ecosystem partners to position NVIDIA as their trusted AI transformation partner.

  • Lead a robust pipeline connected to priority initiatives: digital twins for planning, VLM-powered video analytics, agentic AI for public service automation, and sovereign AI strategies for local governments

  • Engage with various NVIDIA technology partners and identify areas of collaboration from technical to business needs.

  • Influencing industry standards and guidelines, helping build policy, governance models, and responsible AI approaches across European and EMEA public-service markets.

  • Driving talent development and local capacity building, helping cities create innovation hubs and develop the next generation of public-sector AI skills

What we need to see:

  • 8+ years of proven ability in technology systems, AI platforms, cloud/edge software, or vertical public-sector transformation.

  • Experience working with public-sector entities, including local government, city councils, ministries, smart-city authorities, urban mobility agencies, or critical infrastructure operators.

  • Strong negotiation, opportunity management, and deal-closing abilities.

  • Ability to build influence across political, technical, and operational collaborators.

  • Excellent communication and executive-presence skills, with the ability to present sophisticated AI concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Leadership skills: self-starter, autonomous, high integrity, and collaborative.

  • Ability to travel across EMEA.

  • Language requirements: Proficient in English, German.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Proven success with large city or national digital-transformation projects.

  • Experience delivering AI or digital twin outcomes with measurable community impact.

raw.description:
About MedeAnalytics

MedeAnalytics is the Enterprise Healthcare Performance company that delivers AI-driven, cloud-native solutions to help payers, risk-bearing providers and other value- and risk-bearing entities measurably improve performance by reducing costs, improving quality and MLR, optimizing utilization, increasing reimbursement, and elevating care quality across all lines of business. Its enterprise health data management platform—built on its proprietary Health Fabric™—unifies clinical, claims, financial, and social data into a single, scalable source of truth that fuels insights, action, and AI.

As the industry’s healthcare intelligence partner of choice for more than 30 years, MedeAnalytics combines its platform, cross-domain enterprise analytics, AI-powered workflows, and Strategic Advisory™ services to transform intelligence into accountable execution—delivering greater ROI across value-based care, risk and quality, cost and utilization management, and network optimization.

MedeAnalytics empowers organizations to move faster from insight to impact with confidence and measurable results. To learn more, visit medeanalytics.com and follow MedeAnalytics on LinkedIn and Facebook.

About Our Opportunity

The Business Analyst is a client-facing role that leads the implementation and ongoing use of cloud-based data and analytics solutions for MedeAnalytics healthcare payer and provider clients. This role combines business analysis, data integration, and analytics design to help clients use their data effectively. You will lead requirements gathering, translate business needs into technical and data requirements, guide client data onboarding, and coordinate with internal teams to deliver solutions that align with each client’s business model. After go-live, you will continue to lead client support by responding to analytics questions, investigating data issues, and identifying practical improvements.

You will work closely with senior Business Analysts, Project Managers, Client Services, Product, Engineering, BI, and QA teams. You will contribute to process improvements, maintain clear documentation, and build the subject matter expertise needed to manage increasingly complex client needs.

Key Responsibilities:

Client Engagement & Requirements

  • Act as the primary Business Analyst for client onboarding, production support, and analytics discussions.
  • Lead client-facing and internal meetings to gather, clarify, and document business requirements.
  • Translate business needs into clear functional, technical, and data requirements for delivery teams.
  • Define and recommend metrics, dimensions, reports, and analytic outputs for payer or provider use cases.
  • Build productive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders and communicate status, risks, and open questions.

Data Integration & Technical Support

  • Guide clients through secure data ingestion using SFTP, REST APIs, and cloud storage such as AWS S3.
  • Partner with Engineering and data teams to validate successful data landing, transformation, and processing in cloud platforms such as AWS, Snowflake, and Trino.
  • Assist with reconciling datasets and documenting data lineage from source to target.
  • Use SQL and basic Python scripts to support data validation, investigation, transformation, and repeatable analysis.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of requirements, decisions, client-specific configurations, data flows, and test results.

Analytics Design & Validation

  • Lead the design and validation of dimensional models, metrics, and OLAP cubes for healthcare analytics, including cost and utilization, risk adjustment, and quality.
  • Lead business requirements, design input, and validation for dashboards and reports developed in tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or Looker.
  • Perform data analysis to identify trends, validate results, and support client and internal decision-making.

Post-Go-Live Support & Continuous Improvement

  • Respond to client inquiries promptly and communicate findings, next steps, and resolution status clearly.
  • Investigate data and reporting issues, document findings, and coordinate resolution with Engineering, BI, Product, and QA teams.
  • Identify opportunities to improve data quality, reporting structures, metric definitions, and team processes.
  • Lead or contribute to internal initiatives that improve onboarding, documentation, delivery consistency, and client experience.

Essential Skills, Experience and Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience required.
  • Minimum 2 years of experience in business analysis, client services, healthcare analytics, consulting, or a related role; SaaS experience preferred.
  • Working knowledge of healthcare terminology and data, including claims, diagnosis and procedure codes, eligibility, provider, and transaction data.
  • Experience gathering requirements, documenting workflows, writing user stories or acceptance criteria, and supporting testing or issue resolution.
  • Working proficiency in SQL and basic proficiency in Python for data validation and analysis.
  • Exposure to cloud data platforms such as AWS, Snowflake, or Trino preferred.
  • Familiarity with data integration methods such as SFTP, REST APIs, and cloud storage.
  • Experience with Jira or another ticket-based work tracking system.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and Teams.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, organization, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills.

Additional Information:

MedeAnalytics believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is $100,000 - $120,000. Although this position is not bonus eligible, employees receive a comprehensive Total Rewards package that extends beyond base compensation. Please note that actual compensation for all roles may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, relevant work experience, professional achievements/qualifications, skill level, business need, and location, and will be finalized at the time of offer.

Benefits Include:

  • Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage – Effective the first of the month following your start date
  • Company-Paid Life & AD&D Insurance, plus Short-Term and Long-Term Disability (STD/LTD)
  • Company-Paid Employee Assistance Program (EAP) premium tier for your wellbeing
  • 401(k) Plan with company match
  • Paid Holidays and Paid Time Off (PTO)Accruals
  • Employee Referral Bonus Program
  • Professional Development Opportunities to support your growth
  • And More!

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, national origin, gender, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or parental status, disability, veteran status, or other class protected by applicable law. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

Candidates must be authorized to work in the country where this position is located; we are unable to provide or transfer sponsorship.

MedeAnalytics values committed, inspired, and passionate team members. If you’re looking to make an impact doing work that matters, you’re in the right place. Help us shape the future of healthcare by joining #TeamMede.

Important notices:

  • We do not use outside vendors/agencies — please no unsolicited calls or invites.

  • All MedeAnalytics job opportunities are posted exclusively on our Careers Page or trusted partner job boards. Any other communications claiming to be from us are not legitimate. Always verify opportunities before sharing personal or financial information.

raw.description:
Operations Manager

ABOUT US

UpStart brings bold Jewish ideas to light. For nearly two decades, we've partnered with 250+ organizations and thousands of leaders, connecting impact-driven entrepreneurs to the expertise, community, and capital they need to turn ideas into enduring impact.

UpStart was founded with a sole focus: to accelerate the success of social entrepreneurs fueling a renaissance in Jewish life. Today, we're moving from just program provider to field catalyst — shaping how the entire Jewish innovation ecosystem learns, builds, and grows together. We're actively implementing our FY27–29 Strategic Plan, which puts social entrepreneurs at the center of everything we do and codifies our Jewish Social Innovation & Entrepreneurship (JSIE) Methodology as a shared language for the field.

INCLUSIVE HIRING COMMITMENT

UpStart is an equal opportunity employer, and all individuals are encouraged to apply without regard to race, color, religion, age, disability, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, ancestry, genetic information, medical condition, veteran status, or any other class protected under federal, state, or local laws. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and identities to apply, even if you don't meet 100% of the qualifications listed.

POSITION SUMMARY

UpStart is seeking an Operations Manager who brings strong organization, detailed follow-through, and a systems-minded approach to our fast-paced environment. This role partners closely with our fiscal sponsorship, earned revenue, development, and finance work, serving as the operations partner those teams can rely on for process creation, systems support, and project management.

The Operations Manager will build and improve the tools, standard operating procedures, and data practices that help these teams work smoothly and deliver a consistent, high-quality experience for our clients and partners. This person will keep cross-team projects moving, follow up on meeting outcomes, and look for ways to unify how we bring on and support clients across our revenue programs.

This role sits on the Central Operations team, which serves as the operations partner to UpStart’s internal departments. This role will report to the Managing Director, Operations & Systems, and work closely with all internal departments. This role is expected to travel up to 3 times a year for the annual UpStart staff gathering and other meetings as needed.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Project Management and Operational Systems

  • Manage a variety of organizational projects across fiscal sponsorship, earned revenue, development, and finance, keeping timelines, owners, and next steps clear.
  • Coordinate processes across cross-departmental teams, including leading meetings or agenda items.
  • Own meeting follow-up: capture action items, create and track Trello cards, check in when work is late, and ensure the right teams are oriented to what's been decided.
  • Coordinate requests and deliverables with external partners, including our marketing firm and evaluation partners, so materials, data, timelines, and approvals move smoothly.
  • Identify inefficiencies within current processes and implement improvements to optimize workflow. Create and adapt resources and templates to support standard operating procedures.
  • Support staff in adopting new procedures through hands-on guidance and follow-up, and create guides and resources that help colleagues work independently.
  • Keep timelines, processes, and resources organized in internal systems, including Google Drive, Trello, and Salesforce.
  • Help design and maintain automations (for example, in Zapier) that reduce manual work across teams.
  • Support user adoption and training of new tools and systems.
  • Use AI and other technology tools thoughtfully to improve how teams work, and help colleagues do the same.

Fiscal Sponsorship Operations

  • Support the full operations lifecycle of fiscal sponsorship, from first interest through onboarding and beyond, with attention to both the partner experience and the staff experience.
  • Build standard operating procedures, tools, and systems that make it easier for staff to bring on new fiscal sponsees and that ease the workload as the program scales.

Earned Revenue and Revenue Operations

  • Build tools and processes that support staff and elevate the experience we offer our earned revenue clients.
  • Partner with the earned revenue lead on projects in their portfolio, providing project management and operational support.
  • Serve as a thought partner on revenue operations, finding shared approaches to how we bring on and support clients across earned revenue and fiscal sponsorship.

Development Operations

  • Act as a key operations partner to the development team, supporting the processes behind grants and donations.
  • Support colleagues in building and documenting standard operating procedures.

This job description is intended to convey information essential to understanding the scope of the position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of skills, efforts, duties, or responsibilities associated with the position.

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • 3-5 years of experience with project management, operations, and/or process and systems improvement, ideally supporting revenue-generating teams (earned revenue, fundraising, or client services)
  • Strong project management skills, including building project plans and boards from the ground up (we use Trello) and managing projects through completion, keeping owners, timelines, and next steps on track across several projects at once
  • Ability to break down a high-level vision into implementable action items in a fast-paced environment with many projects, moving pieces, and competing priorities
  • Successful collaborator across departments and teams, with a relationship-driven approach to work
  • Excellent communication skills across all seniority levels and stakeholder groups
  • Comfort with technology and openness to using AI tools in daily work; experience with project management systems
  • Experience with a CRM (Salesforce preferred) and with automation tools such as Zapier is a plus
  • Background in any of the following is a plus but not required: revenue operations, marketing, data and evaluation, or nonprofit finance processes
  • Detail-oriented with strong follow-through, while maintaining adaptability and agility as organizational and technological priorities change
  • Exposure to AI-powered tools or interest in deploying them
  • Excitement to learn new skills, technology, and information
  • Commitment to leading through a lens of community and belonging
  • Passion for UpStart’s mission and the work of UpStart’s network
  • Commitment to upholding UpStart’s values and Guiding Principles Regarding Client and Program Partnerships.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

UpStart sets salaries using biennial labor market benchmarking, conducted by an independent third-party partner, based on rates of pay at similar Bay Area organizations. Aligned with this practice, and in support of upholding internal equity, we don’t negotiate salaries. The starting annual salary for this role is $70,000.

In addition to a competitive salary, UpStart currently offers the following benefits:

  • A comprehensive benefits package, including 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance.
  • Life, short-term, and long-term disability insurance.
  • 16 weeks of paid parental leave with no waiting period.
  • 100% employer-funded Health Reimbursement Arrangement (HRA) for medical-related travel, up to $1,950 per year.
  • FSA and Commuter Benefits accounts.
  • Employer-sponsored 401K with employer match.
  • Flexible discretionary paid time off.
  • Annual $1,500 professional development stipend.
  • One-time $300 office setup stipend and provided Mac.
  • Monthly $50 cell phone stipend.
  • 3:00pm local close-of-business on Fridays.
  • Days off for all work-prohibitive Jewish holidays, in addition to secular US holidays.
  • A one-month (30 days) paid sabbatical per every five years of employment.
  • Occasional travel for meetings, conferences, and other business-related activities.
  • A great workplace culture! Check out our culture deck here.

HOW TO APPLY

Use the fields below to submit your resume and a thoughtful, one-page cover letter to our hiring team.

UpStart is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, UpStart will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided accommodations. If accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact Sydney Hirsch, Managing Director, People & Culture at for assistance.

WHAT TO EXPECT

We are committed to a fair and respectful hiring process, and we do our absolute best to respond to every applicant. We prioritize communication and transparency with all candidates, even those who are not moving forward.

Here’s an overview of our hiring process*:

  • Step 1: Apply with your resume and cover letter!
  • Step 2: Phone screen with an UpStart recruiter.
  • Step 3: Video interview with the hiring manager.
  • Step 4: A video interview with a panel of UpStart employees.
  • Step 5: We’ll check your references to learn about your past experience.
  • Step 6: Get an offer letter, sign it, and start your professional journey with UpStart!

*Note: Some of our hiring processes may vary, and not all candidates will advance to each step.

raw.description:
At WelbeHealth, we serve our communities’ most vulnerable seniors through shared intention, pioneering spirit, and the courage to love. These core values and our participant focus lead the way no matter what.

The Coding Auditor & Educator is accountable for ensuring coding is accurate and properly supported by clinical documentation within the health record. This role is focused on production-based coding activities and attainment of coding performance metrics to meet established coding productivity and quality standards.

This role is different because the Coding Auditor & Educator at WelbeHealth:

  • Plays a critical role in ensuring accurate and complete risk-adjustment coding by reviewing clinical documentation, identifying coding discrepancies and missed opportunities, and supporting compliant capture of participant diagnoses and Hierarchical Condition Categories (HCCs)
  • Partners with providers, coders, and cross-functional teams to strengthen documentation quality, improve coding accuracy, and deliver education that supports compliant coding practices, accurate risk adjustment, and better participant outcomes

We care about our team members. That’s why we offer:

  • Medical insurance coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
  • Work/life balance - We mean it! 17 days of personal time off (PTO), 12 holidays observed annually, and 6 sick days
  • 401K savings + match
  • Comprehensive compensation package including base pay and bonus
  • And additional benefits!

On the day-to-day, you will:

  • Assist with retrospective and concurrent coding for PACE Dual participants
  • Conduct pre-visit chart preparations and post-visit chart reviews to identify documentation and coding opportunities that support complete and accurate code capture for all clinical encounters for dual participants, ensuring accurate and complete capture of all reportable diagnoses and HCCs
  • Identify coding discrepancies including unsupported diagnoses, missed coding opportunities, incorrect code assignment, insufficient specificity, and documentation deficiencies
  • Maintain knowledge of and adhere to applicable regulatory requirements, CMS and AMA coding requirements, ICD-10-CM coding guidelines, risk-adjustment guidance, and organizational coding policies and procedures
  • Collaborate with providers through appropriate clinical documentation queries and education to improve documentation specificity, support accurate coding, and ensure all clinically relevant conditions are captured
  • Participate in provider education activities focusing on documentation improvement, coding accuracy, HCC capture, and compliance with regulatory requirements
  • Partner with leadership to identify trends, documentation gaps, and opportunities for provider and coder education that enhance coding outcomes and risk adjustment performance

Job requirements include:

  • Associate’s degree preferred; three (3) years of relevant experience may be substituted
  • Must have an active CCS, CCS-P, CPC, CPC-H CPMA or CRC credential
  • Minimum of four (4) years of experience (or a combination of healthcare-related education and experience) in coding and auditing
  • Minimum of two (2) years of Risk Adjustment (HCC) coding experience in a managed care environment
  • Strong knowledge of ICD-10 coding standards
  • Strong attention to detail to ensure complete and compliant documentation
  • Strong interpersonal and organizational skills
  • Experience in correct application of M.E.A.T. concepts
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint)

We’re seeking a detail-oriented, collaborative Coding Auditor & Educator who is passionate about coding accuracy, clinical documentation integrity, risk adjustment, and helping providers capture the full picture of participant health. If you’re ready to make an impact while supporting our mission and the communities we serve, we’d love to hear from you!

Compensation consists of base salary plus bonus. WelbeHealth offers a competitive total rewards package that includes a 401(k) match, comprehensive healthcare coverage, and a broad range of additional benefits. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience and relevant qualifications.

WelbeHealth maintains required infection control and PPE standards and has requirements relevant to all team members regarding vaccinations.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At WelbeHealth, we embrace and cherish the diversity of our team members, and we're committed to building a culture of inclusion and belonging. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer. People seeking employment at WelbeHealth are considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, age, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information or characteristics (or those of a family member), pregnancy or other status protected by applicable law.

As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next.

We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.

Why You’ll Love This Role

Cribl is seeking Technical Support Engineers to ensure customer success by providing enterprise-level support to our customers and partners. We are a fast-growing, remote-first company with a mission to unlock the value of all observability data. In this role, you will be joining a highly technical and collaborative team that is committed to shipping high quality software and enjoying all the goat gifs the internet has to offer. As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will…

• Performs review and analysis of centralized, aggregated data to identify potential signals and trends in predefined risk indicators.

  • Reviews the effectiveness of implemented actions and escalates concerns when additional action may be required.
  • Evaluates the quality and integrity of study site practices related to protocol compliance and applicable regulations based on centralized monitoring outputs.
  • Maintains effective project-level communication with relevant stakeholders regarding centralized monitoring findings and follow-up activities.
  • Maintains relevant project documentation and contributes to the development and maintenance of centralized monitoring documentation, as applicable.
  • Attends study kick-off meetings, recurring project meetings and other relevant meetings according to project needs.
  • Maintains knowledge of applicable company SOPs, processes and centralized monitoring requirements
  • Education - BA/BS degree in a Life Science field, or equivalent education and experience in line with country-specific requirements
  • Minimum of 1 year of experience in clinical research or a related field
  • Understanding of Risk Based Quality Management and centralized monitoring principles.
  • Working knowledge of applicable clinical research regulations, ICH-GCP principles
  • Ability to review and interpret clinical study data, trends and risk indicators.
  • Good analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively within cross-functional study teams.
  • Good organizational skills and ability to manage activities across assigned studies

When you join Ergomed Group, you make a difference by helping to bring safe and effective pharmaceutical treatment to patients around the world. You’ll join a passionate and collaborative team of experts in clinical research, pharmacovigilance, and quality consulting.

We are diverse in many ways, yet our values unite us. Our values are how we work, not words on a wall. If they sound like you, you will feel at home here.

  • Quality: we hold ourselves to the standard patients deserve.
  • Integrity and trust: we do the right thing, especially when it is hard.
  • Drive and passion: we care about the outcome, because someone is waiting on it.
  • Agility and responsiveness: we move quickly, because patients cannot wait.
  • Belonging: everyone is welcome, and every voice counts.
  • Collaborative partnerships: we go further by going together.

We look forward to welcoming your application.

Medicine moves forward here. So will you.

Ergomed is a specialist clinical research organization focused on rare disease and select oncology indications. We focus on the most complex trials, the studies where experience, judgement, and rigorous operational accountability make the biggest difference. We partner with small to midsize biotech companies to move promising therapies through early phase development, so they reach the patients sooner.

We choose complex work on purpose. Rare disease and oncology trials carry real operational risk, and our people are experts at reducing it, protecting timelines, data quality and the experience of sites and patients at the same time. It is demanding, meaningful work, and no one here forgets that patients cannot wait.

That is why culture matters to us as much as capability. We have built a collaborative, international team where people share ideas, grow their careers and are trusted to take ownership early. With colleagues across North America, South America, Europe, Asia and Australia, we value teamwork, flexibility and a real commitment to work-life balance, because good science comes from people who feel supported.

If you want work with purpose, the agility to make an impact and a team that cares about the people behind the work as much as the work itself, we would love to hear from you.

Welcome to Whataburger Careers!

Our Flavor — Why Whataburger

Whataburger isn’t just a fast-food burger chain it is where bold leadership starts — and where potential doesn’t just grow, it heatsup. Whether you're leading the line or working behind the scenes, this is the place where opportunities stack up, and every day gives you a chance to Make a Difference.

Since 1950, we’ve invested in people who lead with integrity, Serve with Heart, and bring their best flavor to the team. We believe in working together, speaking up, having a little fun, and Winning as One — because great burgers (and great teams) start with the right ingredients. If you're ready — to learn, grow, impact, and Move Forward Boldly — we’ve got your back and your path cooked to perfection.

Your Recipe for Impact — What You’ll Do

As a Consumer and Market Insights Director, you will lead the strategy and execution of consumer, customer, category, and market intelligence efforts that shape the future of Whataburger. By transforming research and data into actionable business recommendations, you’ll help leaders make informed decisions that strengthen the brand, elevate the customer experience, and accelerate growth. In this role, you’ll Make a Difference by uncovering insights that drive meaningful business outcomes, Serve with Heart by championing the voice of the consumer in every decision, Win as One by partnering across the organization to align insights with strategy, and Move Forward Boldly by identifying emerging opportunities, challenging assumptions, and helping the business stay ahead of changing consumer and market dynamics.

Day-to-Day Ingredients — Responsibilities

As a Consumer and Market Insights Director, you will:

  • Lead consumer and market research initiatives that support business strategy.
  • Translate insights into actionable recommendations and business decisions.
  • Partner with Marketing, Operations, Finance, and Innovation leaders to solve business challenges.
  • Oversee qualitative and quantitative research programs.
  • Manage syndicated research, competitive intelligence, and market monitoring.
  • Identify consumer, customer, and category trends that influence growth.
  • Develop executive-ready presentations and strategic recommendations.
  • Establish research methodologies, standards, and governance practices.
  • Manage research budgets and external vendor relationships.
  • Champion the voice of the consumer across the organization.
  • Lead, coach, and develop Consumer Insights team members.
  • Oversee performance management and team priorities.

The Sauce — Pay & Perks

As a Consumer and Market Insights Director, you will receive:

  • Competitive Weekly Pay
  • Relocation package provided
  • Bonus Program
  • 5 weeks of PTO Starting on Day One
  • Paid Corporate Holidays
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • 401(k) match $1/$1 up to 4%
  • Competitive Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefits
  • Short-term and Long-term Disability Benefits
  • Opportunities for Career Development and Growth
  • Whataburger Family Foundation - Scholarship Program (dependents also eligible) and Hardship Grant Assistance
  • Discounted Meals for You and a Guest
  • Cell Phone Service Discounts
  • Computer & Software Discounts
  • Fitness / Gym Discounts
  • Awards and recognition for all you do
  • Retirement Celebration Program

What You Bring to the Table — Required Experience

As a Consumer and Market Insights Director, you must have:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience.
  • 10+ years of experience in consumer insights, market research, strategy, or related fields.
  • Experience leading qualitative and quantitative research programs.
  • Expertise translating research into actionable business strategies.
  • Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience presenting insights and recommendations to senior leaders.
  • Knowledge of consumer behavior, market trends, and competitive intelligence.
  • Experience managing research budgets and vendor partnerships.
  • Strong cross-functional leadership and influence skills.
  • Experience leading, developing, and mentoring high-performing teams.

Extra Toppings — Desired Experience

As a Consumer and Market Insights Director, we prefer you to have:

  • Experience in restaurant, retail, hospitality, or consumer-facing industries.
  • Expertise leveraging syndicated data sources and advanced research methodologies.
  • Experience supporting brand strategy, innovation, pricing, or customer experience initiatives.
  • Proven success building enterprise insights capabilities and governance frameworks.
  • Strong executive storytelling and presentation skills.
  • Experience integrating multiple data sources into cohesive business recommendations.
  • Advanced knowledge of customer segmentation and consumer trend analysis.
  • Experience leading insights functions through periods of growth and transformation.
  • Master’s degree in Marketing, Business, Consumer Research, Analytics, or a related field.

Where & How You’ll Work

This role is designated as remote, offering flexibility to work from your home office. In this role, you’ll have strong collaboration with leadership, across cross-functional teams, and with external partners to align capabilities with restaurant realities. The work environment is fast‑paced and requires sound judgment, strategic thinking, and strong collaboration skills. Full‑time availability is required, with occasional extended hours based on business needs, along with occasional travel to properties, project sites, and external meetings.

raw.description:
Responsibilities

  • Review annotators’ ACCEPT/REJECT decisions and reject reason codes, with a focus on preventing false matches and false rejects.
  • Sample-check or fully review high-risk rows (multiple codes, OTHERS, rows with uncertainty notes).
  • Correct errors, give feedback to annotators, and identify recurring error patterns to keep rule interpretation consistent.
  • Compile questions for the client where rules are ambiguous, and maintain a clarification log.
  • Validate structural compliance of deliverables: every input row returned exactly once and unchanged, timestamps, exact decision and code spelling, correct separators, valid CSV, identifiers preserved as text.
  • Track and report accuracy, review coverage, known limitations, and unresolved rows to support the summary report.
  • Monitor progress to ensure on-time delivery.

Requirements

- At native proficiency level of Korean.

  • 1+ years of experience in data annotation, content moderation, or QA; team lead or training experience preferred.
  • Strong judgment on edge cases, with the ability to explain decisions clearly.
  • Clear communication and the ability to give constructive feedback.

Nice to have

  • Experience building evaluation sets, analyzing accuracy, or managing annotation quality.
  • Understanding of AI-assisted annotation workflows and associated risk controls.

VPN and Location Verification: What You Need to Know

1. Application and onboarding: no VPN. Please do not use a VPN when you apply or go through onboarding.

2. Production: VPN required. Once production starts, you will need to use a VPN. Opera browser is recommended. (Opera is a free built-in VPN and needs no extra installation.) We will send you setup instructions before production begins.

3. Which VPNs are allowed. Standard consumer VPNs are fine. High-risk proxies are not permitted.

4. Periodic checks in Production. For administrative reasons, we may occasionally ask you to access AI Trainer platform without your VPN so we can check your unmasked IP.

raw.description:
Senior Counsel, M&A

Primarily remote · Offices in New York and San Francisco

We’re looking for a Senior Counsel, M&A who wants to help define what it means to practice law in the AI era. At General Legal, you’ll learn how to practice at a firm that’s redefining the future of law: pairing deep M&A judgment with AI-native workflows, and building the playbooks, tools, and habits that the next generation of lawyers will take for granted. We don’t believe you have to choose between quality and speed. Talented attorneys, equipped with the right tools, produce outstanding work faster than most people think possible. If you want to help prove that point, and sharpen your own practice in the process, we’d like to talk.

About General Legal

General Legal is an AI-native law firm built to deliver high-quality legal work faster and more predictably than traditional firms’ hourly billing models. We combine experienced, U.S.-barred attorneys with AI-native workflows to handle drafting, review, and negotiation end to end, without billable hours.

We operate like a startup because we are one. That means modern tooling, outcome-based pricing, remote-friendly work, and meaningful ownership for the people doing the work. By using AI to handle the routine parts of legal work, we give our attorneys the space to focus on judgment, negotiation, and advising over 600 clients on what actually matters.

We’re building a modern law firm where great lawyers can do their best work, and help reshape how legal services are delivered.

Our Values

General Legal is one team with one set of values:

  • Make Clients the Heroes. Our clients’ legal needs are urgent to them, so they’re urgent to us. We deliver fast, reliable, and exceptional outcomes, and every client deadline is our deadline.
  • Continuously Compound. We use technology to do more with less, so everyone’s work goes further, faster, and better.
  • Kind and Candid. We operate as one team without egos, sharing knowledge, giving credit generously, and celebrating wins.
  • Failure is data. We communicate openly, set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and own our mistakes.

About the Role

We’re looking for an M&A attorney to run transformative corporate transactions for our growing roster of startup clients and their acquirers.

This is an execution-focused, high-output role. You’ll own matters end to end, work directly with founders, management teams, and acquirers, and use AI-native workflows to move faster and more consistently than you could at a traditional firm. You’ll have the autonomy to do excellent work, the support of a team that values craft, and the feeling of being part of a team aligned on growth and accomplishment.

The ideal candidate has deep M&A experience specifically in the startup context (acquisitions of early- and growth-stage companies, acqui-hires, mergers, stock sales, asset deals, joint ventures and company sales to strategic or financial buyers), rather than public company M&A. Both buy-side and sell-side experiences are valued and welcomed.

And if you’re the kind of person who spots an opportunity to improve a product, build out a new practice area, or lead something that doesn’t exist yet, we’re always listening.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead M&A transactions end to end for startup clients and their acquirers, including stock and asset acquisitions, mergers, joint ventures, acqui-hires, earnout structures, IP-driven asset deals, and company sale processes, from diligence and LOI through signing and closing.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for clients, advising founders and management teams on the corporate, employment, IP, and governance issues that come up in a deal and at each stage of growth.
  • Negotiate efficiently and to a close. Work directly with buyer-side and seller-side counsel, drawing on your knowledge of market M&A terms to move deals forward and knowing which points are worth pushing on.
  • Advise clients directly on risk and strategy, translating legal complexity into clear, practical guidance for founders and business stakeholders.
  • Leverage AI tools as a genuine force multiplier, and use them critically. Use the firm’s AI legal technology daily to raise the quality of your work and compress timelines, and help refine our workflows and playbooks. Treat AI as a partner in your strategic thinking and learning, not a replacement for it: interrogate its output, pressure-test its reasoning against your own judgment, and use it to explore issues more deeply and get sharper, faster.
  • Raise the bar on our M&A practice. Work within established practice standards and help improve our deal playbooks, checklists, and templates over time. Contribute to the improvement and/or building of our growing M&A tools to enhance your practice and service to our clients.
  • Contribute beyond your lane. Flag a product gap, propose a better process, or raise your hand to lead a new workstream. We value attorneys who bring a “yes, and” orientation to the work.

What We’re Looking For

Background & Experience

  • D. from an accredited law school; active bar membership in good standing in at least one U.S. jurisdiction
  • 4+ years of M&A experience, or fewer years if you can make a compelling case. What matters most is that you have run deals and feel confident doing so, not just supported them.
  • M&A experience rooted in the startup ecosystem: acquisitions of early- and growth-stage companies, acqui-hires, asset deals, and founder exits to strategic or financial buyers. Private M&A experience is strongly preferred over public company M&A.
  • Solid working knowledge of M&A deal mechanics, including purchase agreements, disclosure schedules, reps and warranties, indemnification, and escrow and earnout structures, as well as the ancillary employment, IP, and commercial issues that arise in a transaction.
  • Enough deals under your belt to know what “market” means and move through a transaction without hand-holding.
  • Experience at a leading emerging companies firm (e.g., Cooley, Orrick, Fenwick, Wilson Sonsini, Gunderson, Goodwin, Latham, or similar) is preferred.

How You Work

  • You are good, thorough and fast
  • You use AI tools in your practice today, not theoretically, and you use them critically: to sharpen your analysis and accelerate your learning, never as a substitute for your own judgment
  • You produce clean, sophisticated work product
  • You communicate directly, be that to colleagues/opposing counsel or to the client: clear recommendations, appropriate caveats, no filler
  • You’re self-directed and don’t need hand-holding, but you collaborate well and know when to loop people in
  • You build relationships and earn trust with our valuable non-lawyer talent, including marketing, operations, finance, and product people

Bonus Points

  • You’ve built or improved a legal intake, playbook, or contracting process from scratch
  • You have a vertical or subject matter you’d love to grow or lead
  • You’ve mentored junior attorneys or contributed to team development in a meaningful way

The Structure

This is a remote-first role with annual in-person on-sites for team collaboration, planning, and the occasional celebration. We take the on-sites seriously, and otherwise trust you to do your best work from wherever you do your best work.

On-Call Hours & Responsiveness. Responsiveness is core to how we serve clients. You’ll set your on-call hours by sharing your preferred weekly availability with us, and client matters are routed to you within those hours. Your schedule carries over week to week unless you submit an update, and planned time off during your hours requires at least one week’s notice. During your on-call hours, you’re expected to be available and highly responsive to both clients and our triage team: reviewing your matters at the start, middle, and end of each shift, acknowledging matters promptly with next steps and a timeline, and flagging in advance if you need to step away or a deadline needs to move.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base salary of $200,000 – $240,000 per year, commensurate with experience
  • Potential for meaningful bonus opportunities, which may include equity
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance, 100% covered for you, with 50% medical coverage for dependents
  • Basic Life Insurance premiums fully covered
  • 401(k) with a 5% employer match
  • Unlimited PTO (we encourage at least two weeks a year), plus 12+ paid company holidays
  • 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave, with an additional 4 weeks for the primary caregiver
  • $500 annual wellness budget, plus a $500 budget to set up your workspace
  • Annual state bar fees covered in up to two jurisdictions
  • Weekly lunches
  • Annual in-person on-sites
  • Modern tooling. No billable hours.

Why This Role

We’ve built a legal team that operates like a high-functioning business unit: principled about quality, unsentimental about inefficiency, and genuinely excited about where the tools are going. We’re not looking for someone to grind; we’re looking for someone who’s good enough that they don’t have to.

If you’ve been waiting for a role that matches your ability to produce at a high level without sacrificing the rest of your life, we want you to apply.

How to Apply

Send us your resume along with a few sentences on the M&A work you’ve been doing lately, one example of an M&A deal you drove to a good outcome largely on your own, and why General Legal caught your interest. We read every application.

This role reports to Chris Grogan, our ECVC Partner.

We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team.
